6.13.text:
Article 25

Guidance and supervision as referred to in Article 24 paragraph (2) and paragraph (3), shall be carried out in order to realize the objectives of the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence in accordance with the minimum service standards stipulated by laws and regulations.

Article 3

(1) The implementation of Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence aims to:

a. protect and provide a sense of security for women and children; b. provide services to victims of violence, reporters and witnesses;
c. empower women and children who are victims of acts of violence.
(2) The objectives of implementing the protection of women and children as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. prevention;
b. risk reduction; and
c. handling

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Cimahi City
2. Regional Government is the regional head as an element of the administrator of Regional Government who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Mayor is the Mayor of Cimahi.
4. Regional People's Representative Council, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the regional people's representative institution which is positioned as an element of the administrator of Regional Government.
5. Regional Apparatus is a supporting element of the regional head and DPRD in the administration of Government Affairs that are the authority of the Region.
6. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child who is still in the womb.
7. Woman is a human being of female sex who is legally recognized as a woman.
8. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and community organizations and/or associations.
9. Family is the smallest unit in society that has a marriage relationship consisting of husband, wife, or husband and wife and their child, or father and his child, or mother and her child, or blood family in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
11. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or private life.
12. Protection is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by law enforcement officials and the community towards women and children.
13. Service is an action carried out by professional personnel in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred.
14. Assistance is a process of providing facilitation given by an assistant to a client in identifying needs and solving problems as well as encouraging the growth of initiative in the decision-making process, so that the client's independence on a sustainable basis can be realized.
15. Assistant is a professional social worker who has competence in protection services for women and children. 16. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and society.
17. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with families, communities and Regional Government, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection.
18. Prevention is a direct effort made by the Regional Government to prevent acts of violence against women and children.
19. Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children, hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A, is an integrated service provider institution for victims established by the Regional Government.
20. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to provide protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.

Article 11

(1) The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to implement efforts to protect women and child victims of violence through:

a. implementing protection policies for women and child victims of violence adopted by the government; b. establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and child victims of violence;
c. establishment of P2TP2A;
d. ensuring the implementation of ease of service to victims; e. striving for effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process; and
f. striving to create cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.
(2) The Regional Government in carrying out the obligations and responsibilities as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b, establishes action programs and activities for the protection of women and children in 1 (one) Regional Action Plan.
(3) The Regional Action Plan as referred to in paragraph (2) serves as the basis for Regional Apparatus in implementing protection for women and child victims of violence.
(4) The Regional Action Plan as referred to in paragraph (2) is part of the RPJMD.
(5) The Regional Action Plan as referred to in paragraph (2), is further regulated in the Mayor's Regulation.

CHAPTER VII

PROVISION OF PROTECTION

Article 4

The Scope of this Regional Regulation consists of:

a. protection of women; and
b. protection of children.

Article 26

(1) P2TP2A reports the implementation of the provision of protection for women and children victims of violence to the Mayor. (2) Reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be submitted in writing, covering:

a. administration;
b. finance;
c. services; and
d. performance.
(3) Submission of written reports as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be carried out at least once every 3 (three) months.

Article 28

(1) The Regional Government may provide financial assistance to community organizations, social organizations, or non-governmental organizations and universities that carry out protection for women and children victims of violence.

(2) Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be in accordance with regional financial capacity and implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations in the field of regional finance.

Article 27

Funds for the implementation of protection of women and children victims of violence, are sourced from:

a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget; and/or b. other legal and non-binding sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 13

The obligations of families and parents have obligations and responsibilities in the provision of protection for women and child victims of violence as referred to in Article 10 letters c and d by protecting women and/or children as family members.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Cimahi City
2. Regional Government is the regional head as an element of the administrator of Regional Government who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Mayor is the Mayor of Cimahi.
4. Regional People's Representative Council, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the regional people's representative institution which is positioned as an element of the administrator of Regional Government.
5. Regional Apparatus is a supporting element of the regional head and DPRD in the administration of Government Affairs that are the authority of the Region.
6. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child who is still in the womb.
7. Woman is a human being of female sex who is legally recognized as a woman.
8. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and community organizations and/or associations.
9. Family is the smallest unit in society that has a marriage relationship consisting of husband, wife, or husband and wife and their child, or father and his child, or mother and her child, or blood family in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
11. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or private life.
12. Protection is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by law enforcement officials and the community towards women and children.
13. Service is an action carried out by professional personnel in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred.
14. Assistance is a process of providing facilitation given by an assistant to a client in identifying needs and solving problems as well as encouraging the growth of initiative in the decision-making process, so that the client's independence on a sustainable basis can be realized.
15. Assistant is a professional social worker who has competence in protection services for women and children. 16. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and society.
17. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with families, communities and Regional Government, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection.
18. Prevention is a direct effort made by the Regional Government to prevent acts of violence against women and children.
19. Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children, hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A, is an integrated service provider institution for victims established by the Regional Government.
20. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to provide protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.

a. administration;

c. services; and
d. performance.
(3) Submission of written reports as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be carried out at least once every 3 (three) months.

b. training of P2TP2A members related to the implementation of their duties in preventing violence against women and children.

CHAPTER IX

REPORTING

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Cimahi City
2. Regional Government is the regional head as an element of the administrator of Regional Government who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Mayor is the Mayor of Cimahi.
4. Regional People's Representative Council, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the regional people's representative institution which is positioned as an element of the administrator of Regional Government.
5. Regional Apparatus is a supporting element of the regional head and DPRD in the administration of Government Affairs that are the authority of the Region.
6. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child who is still in the womb.
7. Woman is a human being of female sex who is legally recognized as a woman.
8. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and community organizations and/or associations.
9. Family is the smallest unit in society that has a marriage relationship consisting of husband, wife, or husband and wife and their child, or father and his child, or mother and her child, or blood family in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
11. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or private life.
12. Protection is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by law enforcement officials and the community towards women and children.
13. Service is an action carried out by professional personnel in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred.
14. Assistance is a process of providing facilitation given by an assistant to a client in identifying needs and solving problems as well as encouraging the growth of initiative in the decision-making process, so that the client's independence on a sustainable basis can be realized.
15. Assistant is a professional social worker who has competence in protection services for women and children. 16. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and society.
17. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with families, communities and Regional Government, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection.
18. Prevention is a direct effort made by the Regional Government to prevent acts of violence against women and children.
19. Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children, hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A, is an integrated service provider institution for victims established by the Regional Government.
20. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to provide protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.
